messages:
Alice Kim: incident-bot paging — elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts from Dedicated cluster eu-central-1 (pool: dh-reserved-02). Customer affected: DeltaHealth. Error spike started ~10:12 UTC. Taking initial triage now.

incident-bot: [ALERT] 1779004321 - High 5xx rate on dh-reserved-02 (DeltaHealth). 5xx rate: 18% (baseline 0.7%). Latency p95 increased to 3.2s. See runbook: /runbooks/dedicated-elevated-errors.md

Alice Kim: paging Raj (oncall) and Omar (runtime). Raj — can you join? I’m going to pull SLO-impacting customers list. @DeltaHealth-ops are you seeing customer-side errors?

DeltaHealth-ops: yes, our prod traffic is getting 502/504s for inference calls to model: redwood/gpt-medium-quant. Started ~10:10. We retried from app and saw consistent gateway timeout.

Raj Patel: on it. Jumping to metrics.

Omar Diaz: I’ll look at serving nodes for that pool. Potential noisy neighbor? dh-reserved-02 historically has 4 pods pinned to this tenant.

Tom Erickson: I’m watching autoscale/cluster signals and quota. No recent scale events. CPU on nodes still looks high but not saturated.

Alice Kim: quick customer-impact note: DeltaHealth is processing clinical summarization jobs, ~220 RPS currently. If we don’t mitigate, they'll hit error budget within 30m.

Raj Patel: querying request errors by host and model: ```promql
sum(rate(http_responses_total{cluster="dh-reserved-02",status=~"5.."}[1m])) by (instance,model)
```

Raj Patel: results: 95% of 5xx from instance gpu-node-7 and model redwood/gpt-medium-quant. instance has 5xx spike and high kernel OOM killer events in dmesg.

Omar Diaz: OOM killer? That points to local memory pressure or a buggy process with unbounded allocation. Can someone ssh to gpu-node-7 and dump top / dmesg?

Tom Erickson: running: ```ssh ops@gpu-node-7 sudo journalctl -u inference-runtime -n 200 --no-pager | tail -n 80```

Tom Erickson: logs show frequent process restarts: "out-of-memory: Killed process 32421 (inference-server)" and then kubelet evicting pods. Pod restart loop causing request gateway errors.

Alice Kim: suspected noisy neighbor causing OOM on node — DeltaHealth has pinned heavy batch jobs that may exceed memory footprints when batching spikes occur.

DeltaHealth-ops: we did start a large batch-run at ~10:05 for overnight ingestion. We can pause that job, but it needs confirmation.

Raj Patel: mitigation plan step 1: throttle or pause customer batch job to stop memory blowout. step 2: cordon and drain gpu-node-7 then restart runtime. step 3: shift DeltaHealth traffic to alternate pool (dh-reserved-01) with traffic-swap. step 4: postmortem and capacity recommendation.

Marie Chen: I can contact DeltaHealth ops to request pause. @DeltaHealth-ops do you want us to cut traffic or would you like to pause the batch job yourself?

DeltaHealth-ops: can you pause it? We’ve got no console access right now to heavy-job controller. Pause ASAP.

Omar Diaz: pausing the controller: ```kubectl -n dh-batch scale deployment/dh-batcher --replicas=0 --context=dedicated-eu``` — executing now.

Omar Diaz: done. Observed memory usage drop on gpu-node-7 from 94% -> 48% in ~30s.

sre-bot: Action log: dh-batch paused by Omar Diaz at 10:18 UTC.

Tom Erickson: starting cordon/drain: ```kubectl cordon gpu-node-7 && kubectl drain gpu-node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data```

Tom Erickson: drain in progress. Evicted 3 pods (including inference-server). New pods scheduled to other nodes.

Raj Patel: shifting traffic for DeltaHealth to dh-reserved-01 by updating routing rule in control plane: ```curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/routing/shift" -d '{"tenant":"deltahealth","from":"dh-reserved-02","to":"dh-reserved-01","weight":100}'``` — applying now.

incident-bot: routing update queued.

Raj Patel: routing update applied. Verify health: ```promql
sum(rate(http_responses_total{cluster="dh-reserved-01",tenant="deltahealth",status!~"5.."}[1m]))
```

Raj Patel: DeltaHealth errors dropping to 0.9% on dh-reserved-01, request latency p95 220ms. Good.

Alice Kim: customer-impact update for the record: DeltaHealth saw ~18% error rate at peak, approx 7 minutes of elevated errors before throttling/pausing batch; roughly 5000 failed requests. We should notify CS and runbook owners.

Marie Chen: notifying CS and sending summary to DeltaHealth: "We paused a heavy batch job and shifted traffic to alternate reserved pool to restore service. Root cause: local memory exhaustion on gpu-node-7 due to batch job + runtime memory profile. Our recommended remediation: reduce batch concurrency, add memory limits to batcher, and request a capacity bump or dedicated extra node."

DeltaHealth-ops: appreciate the fast response. We'll adjust batch concurrency and follow up on capacity with your rep.

Omar Diaz: follow-ups for eng-runtime: add better cgroup memory limits and OOM-aware backpressure in runtime. Also add a detection alert for sustained kernel OOM lines.

Raj Patel: doc immediate fixes: 1) add k8s resource limits to dh-batch manifest; 2) create a rule to auto-throttle batchers when node memory >80%; 3) create a routing fallback for tenant traffic if node-level evictions detected.

Tom Erickson: I queued a node restart for gpu-node-7 and removed cordon now that pods are rescheduled.

Alice Kim: handoff — Raj will lead postmortem. Omar will own runtime fixes. Tom will own infra/node-level remediation. Marie will handle customer comms and CS follow-up. I'll mark incident as mitigated and close paging.

Raj Patel: documenting timeline and assigning follow-ups in Ops tasks. ETA for postmortem draft: EOD today.

incident-bot: Incident 1779004321 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Paging cleared.

Alice Kim: thanks all — good coordination. :tada:
